title: Establish reproducible build contracts and layered cache profiles for faster CI
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Our CI times have regressed for several services due to drift in base images, inconsistent layer ordering, and cache misses across runners. This ticket creates an explicit 'build contract' for service repos (a minimal, documented set of expectations about base image digests, pinned toolchain versions, and allowed extra layers) and implements layered cache profiles and a cache-warming pipeline so common rebuilds hit remote cache and developer iteration is faster.

Goals:
- Define a reproducible build contract template that repos adopt (base image digest, canonical layer split, pinned package manager locks, and build flags).
- Produce two canonical base images (runtime-slim and build-tools) with digests published to our internal registry.
- Implement layered cache profiles (hot, warm, cold) and wire them into our remote CAS/BuildKit cache so CI can target the right cache TTLs for different stages.
- Add a scheduled cache-warming job that runs on our buildfleet to pre-populate caches for the top 20 most frequently changed repos.
- Update a sample service (payments-api) to the contract and measure median CI time reduction.

Success metrics / Acceptance criteria:
- Top-20 CI pipelines see at least 30% median wall-clock time reduction on incremental builds within two weeks of rollout.
- Rebuilds from identical commits on different runners produce identical image digests (reproducibility test).
- Documentation and a repo-lint rule are in place; 80% of active services adopt the contract in the next cycle.

Scope & non-goals:
- This ticket focuses on build determinism and cache-first performance; it does NOT include full migration of all repos (that will be follow-ups), nor changes to production deployment workflows except where necessary for image digests.

Technical approach & trade-offs:
- Use BuildKit with content-addressable storage (CAS) as the canonical remote cache. BuildKit allows deterministic layer ordering and better cross-runner cache hits, but requires CI runners to use BuildKit-compatible daemon or the newer moby/buildkit executor. Some legacy runners will be deprecated.
- Create small, audited base images (pinned by digest) to reduce layer churn. Smaller images trade off convenience of heavy base images (less per-repo Dockerfile steps) for faster pulls and stable digests.
- Layered cache profiles: hot (short TTL, for frequently changing node_modules/python wheels), warm (longer TTL for OS packages), cold (rarely changed - heavy compiled caches). TTLs balance cache storage cost vs hit rate.
- Cache-warming job will intentionally pull artifacts and run partial builds for expected CI entrypoints. This increases registry egress and runner time — we'll limit to top-20 projects and stagger schedules to limit cost.

Tasks (rough):
1) Audit 40 highest-traffic repos for Dockerfile variance and existing cache hits.
2) Define and publish build contract template and add conformance checklist.
3) Build and publish two canonical base images; add automated digest rotation policy (manual review for major upgrades).
4) Implement BuildKit-based remote cache integration in CI (GH Actions / internal runner changes).
5) Implement cache profiles and a config knob in repo-level ci.yaml to opt into hot/warm/cold layers.
6) Ship scheduled cache-warm job and monitor hit rates.
7) Migrate payments-api as a canonical example and collect before/after telemetry.

Risks and mitigation:
- Runner incompatibility: provide a compatibility shim and deprecation plan.
- Increased registry storage/egress costs: cap warming to 20 repos and monitor costs.
- Non-conformance across repos: add repo-lint and automation to propose PRs.

comments: 2026-02-17 - Initial audit complete: 42 repos scanned. Common anti-patterns: installing dev deps in runtime image, cache-busting apt update ordering, and mixing build and runtime layers. See audit spreadsheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/ci-audit-2026

2026-02-23 - Design review notes: PM requested explicit rollback workflow for base-image digest updates; Security requested provenance info (SBOM) for canonical images. Action: add SBOM generation step to base-image pipeline.

2026-02-28 - Prototype PR opened to platform repo (PR#6123). Implemented initial BuildKit remote cache integration and a ci.yaml cache profile. Need infra approval for adding new registry lifecycle rules.

2026-03-04 - PR feedback from infra (A. Morales): prefer staged rollouts; don't rotate base-image digest automatically — require manual verification window. Updated PR to include manual approval gate.

2026-03-09 - Payments-api migration testing: incremental build time dropped from 8m42s -> 4m12s on average (CI run ids: https://app.ci.redwood.ai/builds/77812). Reproducibility test: identical digest on two different runners for the same commit SHA.

2026-03-12 - Next: finalize canonical base image build pipeline, add SBOM artifact publishing to S3, and schedule cache-warm job for first tranche of 10 repos. Assigned follow-up ENG-121346 to roll out lint fixes across repos.
